heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > What the app does
text: Cohort Coach helps a Grade 3 teacher find the one mistake many of her pupils make, and then helps her fix it. A short check of ten questions shows what children get wrong. Teachers whose classes make the same mistake follow the same three-week track on that one mistake. Before she tries a new way of teaching on real children, she can rehearse it with five simulated children in the Practice Class. Everything in the demo uses simulated data.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > Home
text: Home says how many children you checked this term and what your class's focus is. One button takes you to the next step. The other tiles open Practice, My programme, What I entered, Watch a rehearsal and My profile.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > Enter check
text: You enter what each child wrote on the ten-question check. You can photograph the answer sheets in roll order, or type the answers. The phone shows which boxes it could not read and asks you to confirm them. A sheet photo is read once and not kept, and no child's name is ever entered.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > My class
text: My class shows one card for each mistake that children in your class make. Each card says how many of the children you checked make that mistake, and shows an example from your own class with a drawing of sticks. The card for your class's focus says so. You can tap the speaker to hear a card read aloud, and tap the flag if a card looks wrong.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > Practice
text: Practice is a rehearsal with five simulated children who make your own class's mistakes. You type or speak what you would say to them, and tap materials such as bundles of ten or loose sticks. When you finish, you get private feedback with two things that went well and one thing to try, each quoting your own words. It never gives a score.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > Practice
text: The children are made up, and the rehearsal stays on your phone unless you choose to share it.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > My programme
text: My programme shows where you are in your three-week track, step by step, and which modules come next. Each module is about five minutes and arrives as a voice note. After a module you are asked two quick questions: whether you tried it in class, and how it went.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > What I entered
text: What I entered lists the checks you have entered, with each child's answers on request and whether the results have been sent.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The screens > My profile
text: My profile holds your language, your classes, how much storage and data the app uses, backup and restore, your consent choices, the privacy notice and a feedback form. You can change language here, and you can erase everything.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > The mistakes the app looks for
text: - Writes a number the way it is said: forty-three becomes 403. - Drops the carried ten: 47 plus 25 becomes 62. - Takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column: 52 minus 29 becomes 37. - Borrows a ten but does not reduce the tens digit: 52 minus 29 becomes 33. - Swaps tens and ones: 43 becomes 34. The app notices this one but has no track for it yet.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > Working without signal
text: Most of the app works with no signal. Entering a check, opening saved modules and reading your cards all work offline, and results are sent when the phone finds signal again. The Practice Class needs a connection, and when the signal is weak it falls back to typing.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > Keeping the app on your phone
text: You can save the app on your phone's home screen like any other app. On the first screen, tap How to install and follow the steps. Saving it is optional: it also works in the browser.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > Your privacy
text: No child's name, face or voice is collected. Per-child answers stay on your phone; only counts for your whole class are sent, and only if you agree. The assistant never sees a child's name, and it cannot see other teachers' data.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > What the assistant can and cannot do
text: The assistant answers questions about how to use the app and what its screens mean, using only these help pages. It cites the page it used and tells you how to check. It cannot approve, send or delete anything, it cannot see other teachers, and it will say so when it does not know.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > Does the app use AI, and how does the assistant find its answers?
text: Yes, in a few places, and always with checks. In the Practice Class an AI plays the pretend children and labels the move you made, and after you finish it gives feedback that quotes your own words. Every number about a class is worked out by the app's own code, never by the AI. The assistant uses retrieval-augmented generation, often called RAG. It first searches these help pages for passages about your question, matching both the words and the meaning.

heading: Cohort Coach: how to use the app > Does the app use AI, and how does the assistant find its answers?
text: Then a small AI model writes a short answer using only those passages, and the app checks that every quote really is on the page before it shows you the answer. If the pages do not cover your question, the assistant says so instead of guessing, and each answer lists the page it came from.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > What should I do today
text: Open My programme. It shows the step you are on: the check, your cards, a module, or the next check. Do that one step. If you have not entered a check yet, start with Enter check. If you have, open My class to see your cards, then the module in My programme. Plan for no more than about twenty minutes a week: the app is built around that limit.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > What an error card means
text: A card names one mistake and says how many of your children make it. A child is counted only if the mistake showed on at least two questions that test it, so one slip is not counted. The example under the count comes from your own class. The card never says why a child made the mistake for certain; it only says what is most likely, and a one-minute question you can ask a child to check.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > How is my class doing since the last check
text: The app shows change in children only after the next check, not before. Until then, My programme says "awaiting next check". The number of modules delivered tells you what was sent, not whether children improved. When the next check is entered, My programme shows the comparison.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > I'm stuck, what can I try
text: - Try the module for your class's focus again with only three children, using bundles of ten and loose sticks. - Ask the child to explain how they got their answer before you correct it. - Check by adding back: if 52 minus 29 is 23, then 23 plus 29 should be 52. - Rehearse in Practice first, then try it in class. - Tap the flag on any card that looks wrong, so the team can review it.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Why was this audio chosen
text: A module comes from the track for your cohort's mistake, which a coach has approved. The app picks the module that follows the last one you finished. It does not pick modules by how well you teach, and it never scores a teacher. Each module shows a badge: Checked means the app's automatic checks passed, and Reviewed means a coach also approved it.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > If a module did not work
text: A track that does not work is a fault of the track, not of you. After a module, tap that it did not work, and the team reads it as feedback on the track.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Practice, step by step
text: Open Practice, then Start. Say or type what you would say to the children, for example: "Priya, what is 52 minus 29?" Open Materials to show bundles of ten. When you are done, tap End and see feedback. If you name a real child, the name is removed before anything is sent to the AI; the five pretend children keep their names. Rehearsing is a way to try a move safely.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Practice, step by step
text: No source has shown yet that it changes children's results; the pilot will test that.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Speaking in Practice
text: Hold the button while you speak and let go when you finish. A timer shows how many seconds you have used, up to 25. At 25 seconds the recording stops by itself, with the message "That is the longest we can listen to at once. Say the rest in a second message." What you said in those 25 seconds is still used. A very short or silent recording is not sent: you see "I didn't catch that.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Speaking in Practice
text: Try again." Silence is never scored. Your recording is sent to a speech service (Bodhan AI, or Sarvam if Bodhan cannot) to be turned into text, then dropped; it is never kept. The text of what was heard is always shown. Each pretend child keeps one voice for the whole practice, and the voice sounds happier or sadder as the engine's mood for that child changes. The voices are AI-generated.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Speaking in Practice
text: If the voice stops working, or this practice has used its share of speech, you see "Voice is off for the rest of this practice. The text continues." and you carry on by typing.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Telegram
text: Telegram is planned for later and is not available now. For now, use the web app for every step.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > How do I print a check paper
text: Open Papers, tap Create a paper and choose Generate from rules. Choose the pilot paper (Form A before training, Form B after it), whose answers you can enter on this phone, or a new paper for your class, which you print and mark by hand with its answer key. A new paper is built from your last check's class counts, or from four short questions about your class, or it is the standard paper.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > How do I print a check paper
text: A topic you have not taught is left off the paper, so no child is flagged for it. Pick the language and tap Make the paper. The first ten items are anchors: the same skills and level on every paper, and before and after are compared only on these. Up to five adaptive items go deeper on what your class finds hard; they help find errors and never count as improvement.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > How do I print a check paper
text: A pre-test makes its post-test twin at the same time, frozen until the track ends. Only an approved paper prints; a paper in wording nobody has reviewed yet waits for a reviewer. Once the first sheet is entered, the paper is frozen. All your papers are on the Papers page. No AI writes a paper: code builds it from approved rules.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Papers: make a paper, bring one in, and see what became of it
text: A paper is the printed set of questions; a check is one use of it in your class. They are separate jobs, so you make or bring in a paper on the Papers page, and Enter check only asks you to choose one. Open Papers and tap Create a paper. There are two ways.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Papers: make a paper, bring one in, and see what became of it
text: Generate from rules: code builds the paper from the approved rules, from your last check's class counts, from four short questions about your class, or the standard paper. The first ten items are anchors, the same skills and level on every paper, and before and after are compared only on these; up to five adaptive items go deeper on what your class finds hard and never count as improvement.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Papers: make a paper, bring one in, and see what became of it
text: From a PDF or an answered sheet: upload a PDF or up to three photos of a paper you already used. Only the printed questions are read. Handwriting and names are ignored and not kept, and the upload is deleted when you confirm, or after 24 hours. The AI reads the questions; it never gives an answer key.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Papers: make a paper, bring one in, and see what became of it
text: Code works out every correct answer, the error each item can show and the grid of which items check which error, and a printed key that differs is flagged, never trusted. You confirm every item before the paper can be used. An item the system cannot score yet, such as a word problem, is listed as not supported: leave it out or enter it by hand. A dictated item needs the number that was said.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Papers: make a paper, bring one in, and see what became of it
text: An imported paper says Imported, awaiting review until a reviewer confirms it, and it is not printed by the system because it is already printed. Enter check uses the chosen paper's own key, worked out by code from its numbers, so an imported paper is entered like any other. Once the first sheet is entered the paper is frozen and cannot change: make a new version instead. Each paper shows whether cohorts have formed.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Papers: make a paper, bring one in, and see what became of it
text: If not, it says why and what to do next: no check has used the paper yet, a check is open with some sheets entered, every sheet is entered and not yet approved, approved but not closed, or submitted and waiting for other classes with the same error. A pre-test cannot go to a cohort, because cohorts form from its results. Papers assigned to you show at the top of Papers and in Enter check.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Papers: make a paper, bring one in, and see what became of it
text: The assistant asks one question at a time about anything missing, such as the class, the kind, the form or an unclear number, and fills in the draft from your answers. It marks what it changed with an Undo, and it never confirms, approves or assigns: you press those.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Why did no cohort form?
text: A cohort forms when enough classes share the same track. Each class gets one track: writing a number as it is said (PV-HEARD) first, otherwise the mistake the most children made, and only when at least 1 child in 4 showed it with at least 10 children checked. A child shows a mistake only when it appears on at least 2 of the questions that check it.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Why did no cohort form?
text: The screen gives every class's reason for each mistake: in, under 1 in 4, another track, too few children checked, or no track for that mistake yet. A class that is the first to submit waits for other classes. In production a cohort needs 15 classes (COHORT_MIN_CLASSES). The pilot and the demo allow 2, labelled "Pilot cohort, two classes".

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Why did no cohort form?
text: When a paper has only one question of a kind, such as borrowing across a zero (703 - 468), the 2-question rule cannot be met there. The pilot and the demo may then count that one question (COHORT_ALLOW_SINGLE_ITEM_PROBES), and the cohort says "Based on one question per child". Production leaves this off. At pilot scale there is no waitlist: both classes are trained, and the pilot compares the trained mistake with the untrained ones.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > How is the next module chosen?
text: Code chooses it; the AI only words it. After module 1 the teacher plays it or marks it heard, then answers Tried it, Partly or Not yet, with an optional note (a child's name is removed before it is saved). Then she can press Generate next module, and the coach can press it for her. Tried it gives the next module in the track. Partly gives the same approach again, as a smaller step with more practice.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > How is the next module chosen?
text: Not yet gives another approach for the same mistake from the strategy library, leaving out the approaches she has already had. If she has not answered by the set date (3 days in the demo), the planned next module is queued, and her silence is never counted as a result. Call 5 words the module from the approved module topic and strategies; if no draft comes back, code writes it from the same content.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > How is the next module chosen?
text: Every module goes to the coach's review queue before it reaches her, voiced in her language with her class's numbers filled in by code. A failed voice leaves the text, with a retry.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Entering a check: roll numbers, absent children and finishing
text: Enter check works from a paper that already exists. Choose it (papers assigned to you come first), check the date, say how many papers there are, and tap Start the check. If there is no paper for your class yet, use Create a paper to go to Papers; Enter check never makes one. Then work one roll number at a time.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Entering a check: roll numbers, absent children and finishing
text: The roll list shows each roll number as Not entered, Entered, or Absent, and as Approved or Not approved, with a line of counts above it. Add a sheet by typing the answers, by Take a photo of this sheet, or by Select a folder of pictures (where your phone cannot choose a folder, Choose pictures lets you pick many from the gallery).

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Entering a check: roll numbers, absent children and finishing
text: The AI reads the picture and fills the boxes, marking the ones it is unsure of; it is a suggestion. Tap the small picture icon beside the roll list to see the sheet beside the boxes, compare, correct, and tap Approve. Typed answers need approving too. Tick Absent today for a child who was away; that approves the roll number.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Entering a check: roll numbers, absent children and finishing
text: Under the boxes, tick Missed the teaching for the topics your register says were missed; the question numbers come from the paper. Finish entering is switched on only when every roll number is approved or absent, and a note above it names the ones that are not. Pictures are read and dropped: they are held in memory only and are gone when you finish or leave the page.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Entering a check: roll numbers, absent children and finishing
text: To change something afterwards, open Enter check and tap Reopen, then Finish entering again to update the results.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > When the AI is not available
text: If the AI service is down, the top of the screen says AI: off, and each part that needs it tells you so: type the answers instead of reading a photo, the module comes from the approved template and is shown as text, and your chat question waits for your mentor or coach. Nothing you entered is lost.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Reading the results: answer map, why an error is flagged, what it means
text: Open My class after you finish a check. Under the findings, the answer map has one row for each child (by roll number) and one column for each question. A tick means correct.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Reading the results: answer map, why an error is flagged, what it means
text: Two letters show which mistake the answer matches, with a colour and a pattern: PH writes a number the way it is said, PR swaps tens and ones, AC forgets the carried ten, SF takes the smaller digit from the larger, SN borrows a ten but does not reduce the tens digit. A cross means wrong with no known mistake, a dash means left blank, a question mark means it could not be read.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Reading the results: answer map, why an error is flagged, what it means
text: A dashed edge means the child made the mistake once only, so it is possible, not confirmed. Tap a mistake in the list above the table to highlight it; tap a box to see the answer given, the correct answer and what the child likely did. Under the table, Why an error is flagged shows which questions check each mistake and how many children in your class made it. The table stays on this phone.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Reading the results: answer map, why an error is flagged, what it means
text: What each error means explains each mistake with an example from your class. These explanations are drafts until a coach approves them.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > A cohort for your class and its ideas to try
text: On My class, tap Create a cohort for my class, choose the mistakes to work on (the most common one is chosen for you) and confirm. It is just your class, with no other teachers yet, and only counts are saved. Open the cohort page to read the improvement track: what you are seeing, why children do this, a ten-minute activity, common teaching mistakes, how to know it is working and ideas for home.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > A cohort for your class and its ideas to try
text: The strategies, their steps and examples, the two-minute check and what to do when a module is not working are in the modules above it, one module at a time. Everything is text first. Tap Download audio on a section, or for the whole pack, to get an MP3 file made with an AI-generated voice; it needs a connection, and nothing is made until you tap.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > A cohort for your class and its ideas to try
text: Hindi and Tamil text is not written yet, so those pages show English with a note.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your improvement track: modules
text: Your improvement track is a few short modules, one after another, each with a due date. Module 1 is ready as soon as you start the track. Later modules show only a title and a date until their turn. Use Module 1 in class, then tell us how it went: It worked, It partly worked, Not yet working or I didn't try it yet. Then press Get the next module.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your improvement track: modules
text: Until you answer, that button is closed and says when the next module will arrive by itself. What you answer decides the next module. It worked moves you to the next module in the plan. It partly worked gives the same approach again as a smaller step. Not yet working gives a different approach.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your improvement track: modules
text: I didn't try it yet is a pause, not a result: the module stays open, the next date moves by 7 days (at most twice), and you can pick a reason, read a shorter version or ask your mentor or coach. After the second pause the planned module comes by itself, and Get the next module works whenever you want it.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your improvement track: modules
text: If you do not answer, the next module still comes on its due date, and we do not count the silence as a result. You can answer late: the answer is saved with its module and only changes modules that are not made yet. Each module has Why this module? with the reason, the text you can read or hide, and Download audio. A track has at most six modules.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your improvement track: modules
text: If the plan runs out or the limit is reached, the app tells you to talk to your mentor or coach. When the track is finished it says it is time for the next check. Making a module needs a connection; modules you already have, and audio you downloaded, work offline.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your check-in is private
text: When you answer a module, the answer, your note and any follow-up questions are saved for you alone. A lock on every step says so, and every step has a Skip. Nothing reaches the cohort chat unless you read the exact text and press Share with my cohort. After your answer you may see one or two short questions (or a Skip), then a line that says what changes next, written by the app from what you told us.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your check-in is private
text: Then comes the choice to share a short summary with your cohort. The text is shown in a box you can edit. It is built from your answer, what the app understood from your note, and your note with names removed.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your check-in is private
text: You choose the parts: how it went, your note, what you would like help with, how many children in your class (counts only, off by default) and your chat name (off by default; otherwise it says "A teacher in this cohort"). It never contains a child's name, a roll number, a class code or a percentage, and if you type one the button explains what to remove. Pressing Share twice posts it once.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your check-in is private
text: You can Retract it later, and you can share it later until the next module is made. If you ask for help, your question goes through the normal question flow, where a coach checks any AI draft. If you do not want to share, press Don't share. Coaches and mentors see only how many teachers answered worked, partly, not yet or not tried, never your note, unless you shared it.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > Your check-in is private
text: If your note suggests you or a child may be in difficulty, the app says so gently and shows Ask my coach to call me. Your coach is told only if you press it, and nothing you wrote is sent.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > The cohort chat
text: Under Cohort chat, join your cohort (a separate tap, with your agreement) and you will see one thread with the other teachers, your mentor and your coach. Everyone shows as a label such as Teacher 7, Mentor or Coach, never a name. Ask a question or share a tip. Names, roll numbers, phone numbers and links are hidden before a message is posted, and you are told what was hidden.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > The cohort chat
text: When you ask a question, a mentor or coach may reply. If nobody does in the time shown at the top (30 minutes normally; 5 seconds in the demo), your question, with details hidden, goes to an AI assistant, which answers only from approved material, names its sources and says it is an AI answer. If it has no approved source it says so and a mentor or coach will see your question. A coach can correct the AI answer.

heading: Teacher help: today, when you are stuck, and what the audio is > The cohort chat
text: A reply from another teacher does not stop the AI.
